acceptance: The stable package extends ChangeIntentV1 with deterministic upsert-edge, remove-edge, and remove-node operations while retaining no-op and upsert-node compatibility.

A bounded ChangeIntent may contain multiple operations, applies them in declared order, and rejects duplicate/conflicting targets or a sequence that becomes structurally invalid at any step with stable typed errors.
upsert-edge validates edge shape, endpoint existence, relation/domain compatibility, and rejects an existing edge kind or endpoint change under the same edge id.
remove-edge rejects unknown edge ids; remove-node rejects unknown node ids and refuses removal while incident edges remain unless those edges were removed earlier in the same ordered intent.

Every proposal preserves exact base revision, intent identity/digest, provenance, confidence, ordered operation list, deterministic delta/proposal identity, and a separately validated candidate Product Graph revision.
Compilation is pure and deterministic, does not mutate the base or intent, and produces the same candidate/proposal identity across repeated execution and JSON-key insertion order.
Focused tests plus full format, lint, typecheck, and test suites pass on the exact candidate; Diffcipline, Alibaba OCR, Jev, exact-head CI, and post-merge CI are recorded before closure.

required: Exact base/head/merge-base identities and full changed-file accounting.
Focused tests for edge upsert/removal, node removal, ordered multi-operation application, conflict rejection, domain validation, determinism, and input immutability.
Pinned Diffcipline proof, Alibaba OCR accounting/delegation semantic review, Jev exact-diff judgments, and exact-head Ubuntu/Windows CI.
Post-merge fresh-main CI and canonical CURRENT frontier reconciliation.

minimality.rationale: Extend the already qualified Change Intent compiler in @ineractive/product-graph. No new package, provider, persistence layer, dependency, or model integration is needed for richer graph-operation semantics.

requirements: Compilation remains pure: no network, model inference, clock/randomness dependence, source mutation, database access, capability grant, or external effect.
Operation order is explicit and semantically meaningful; no automatic reordering may hide an invalid intermediate graph state.
Removal is fail-closed: unknown targets and node removal with remaining incident edges are rejected.
Confidence remains evidence only; proposal generation cannot grant authority or accept a candidate as canonical truth.

outcome: The stable @ineractive/product-graph Change Intent compiler can deterministically propose ordered edge/node graph mutations and bounded multi-operation deltas without canonical or source mutation.
rationale: SG-000027 intentionally stopped at no-op and one-node upsert. The canonical next frontier requires edge/remove/multi-operation proposal semantics before natural-language intent interpretation or Question Gate work.

risk.recovery: Revert SG-000028 contract/compiler/test/evidence changes; SG-000027 no-op/upsert-node behavior and all previously qualified Product Graph semantics remain intact.

scope_in: Extend the closed ChangeIntent operation vocabulary with upsert-edge, remove-edge, and remove-node while preserving no-op and upsert-node.
Allow a bounded non-empty ordered operation list and apply operations sequentially against an in-memory candidate graph.
Validate edge shape and stable-id updates, reject duplicate/conflicting operation targets, reject missing removal targets, and reject node deletion while incident edges remain at that step.
Validate structural and Product Graph domain semantics after each operation and again for the final candidate revision.
Return the ordered operation list in ProposedGraphDeltaV1 and bind the deterministic intent/delta/proposal digests to the complete sequence.
Add focused compatibility, multi-operation, edge/remove, determinism, immutability, and fail-closed tests plus closure/frontier evidence.
scope_out: No natural-language/model/provider intent parsing, no Question Gate or Assumption Ledger, and no source-binding or compiler execution.
No canonical Product Graph commit, database migration, Git mutation, network call, credential use, capability grant, or external-effect execution.
No implicit cascade delete, operation reordering, graph merge algorithm, concurrent-intent reconciliation, or automatic conflict resolution.
No new dependency, package, lockfile change, provider-paid inference, or change to existing domain vocabularies.
No claim that later P02-S04/P02-S05 tasks are complete.
